items.title: Bernie Kirsh interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 27, 2022
items.q: I was interviewed to do an album for Patti Smith. She wanted to work at Electric Lady, for the vibe, you know because it was Jimi’s place and so forth. So I went and talked to her and we worked it out and I started doing the recording, and did it

ctx.x: You know it’s funny, those were the techniques in those days, so you didn’t think much about it. I mean subsequently there would be edits that I would attempt to do, and hopefully successfully, that required, you know, slices of a piece of tape. And you might have three or four different tries at it that were all sliced and you’d have to get them in order on the backing with the tape backing so they would play correctly. Because if it didn’t play then you just destroyed something. So you learned these editing…
Am I correct that you recorded Patti Smith’s “Horses” record?
Yeah I did, I did. That was 1975, fall of ’75 I think, October, somewhere in there.
